acceptance.cause: Disposable fake ELF bridge in unit tests lacked POSIX owner execute mode. Windows X_OK behavior hid the fixture defect; Linux correctly rejected it before fake child launch.
acceptance.real_bridge_build: External terminal shows GNU 11.4 build and native preflight succeeded.

source_preservation.cross_host_mileage_note: Only mile_data.txt differs from this Windows copy; this is official controller mileage state and can vary across hosts. The captured runtime separately reports its original Ubuntu source files unchanged. No static official executable/model/library mismatch was found.

native_runs.failure_timing_assessment: SDK connection timeout was the reported primary exception and triggered cleanup. robot_mujoco exited normally with explicit signal-handler shutdown. mc_ctrl ultimately died by SIGABRT (-6); save/terminate tail is consistent with cleanup-time native teardown, but missing pre-cleanup poll means a prior controller abort cannot be ruled out. It is incorrect to call this a Python crash or prove mc_ctrl abort caused the initial timeout.
native_runs.failure_cause: Official mc_ctrl server attempted to bind absent 192.168.234.1 because staged sdk_config target_ip only describes the client feedback endpoint. The official binary separately reads SDK_CLIENT_IP for its own bind interface; the new runtime supplies loopback only to its children.

conclusion: Official dependencies and state publication started, but both actual controller logs show client_ip 192.168.234.1, two Cannot assign requested address bind failures, and sdk init failed. The simulator-side controller SDK therefore did not initialize, explaining client connection timeout before standUp/image control/gait/firing. No native gait or mission acceptance has been achieved.

fixes.runtime_diagnostics_recommendation: Record each owned child poll status immediately before cleanup and the specific signal sent. Preserve -6 as native abort; never silently accept it as clean exit.

limitations: Current audit host is Windows. No new Linux native run was performed.
Existing 0.3.0 records have no pre-cleanup poll/signal ledger, so the exact timing of controller SIGABRT cannot be proven.
Empty Python fault.log does not rule out an abort in a separate native controller process.
